cse-2015-3-cs-10.approach: Find an interleaving that puts both processes in the critical section (breaks mutual exclusion), then note that neither process ever blocks: each loop just re-runs, so deadlock cannot occur.

steps.title: How a process enters
steps.body: X enters its critical section **only while `varQ == true`** (the CS is the body of the inner while loop); Y enters only while `varP == true`. If the condition is false, the process simply goes round the outer `while(true)` again; it never waits.

steps.title: Mutual exclusion fails
steps.body:
Interleaving from varP = varQ = false:

| # | Action | varP | varQ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | X: varP = true | T | F |
| 2 | Y: varQ = true | T | T |
| 3 | X: tests varQ == true → **enters CS** | T | T |
| 4 | Y: tests varP == true → **enters CS** | T | T |

Both are in the critical section at once.

steps.title: No deadlock
steps.body: There is no blocking wait: when the inner condition is false a process leaves the inner loop and continues. Both can never be stuck waiting for each other, so deadlock is prevented. Hence **A**.
